title: What is known about 1RB0LF_0RC1RD_0LD0RA_1RC0RE_1RF---_1LA0LB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LF_0RC1RD_0LD0RA_1RC0RE_1RF---_1LA0LB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves (kernel) that a halt needs the word A>0 1 1 1 (halt_needs_A0111), A stepping onto the front of a train, and proves the sweep that eats one word of a train (sweep_train, for all values of its parameters). No halt in the first 1011 steps (C); in the run, A meets 0 1 1 0 thousands of times but never 0 1 1 1.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: A halt needs A>0 1 1 1
claims.text: Three steps before a halt the head is in state A on a 0 followed by 1 1 1: E (halting on a 1) is entered only from D1, D only from B1, and B from A0 or from F1 (which writes the 0 that D would read).

claims.title: One sweep eats one word of a train
claims.text: From L 1110 (10)^(b+1) 110 110 (10)^(a+1) 11 C> 0^inf the machine reaches L 1010 (10)^(b+1) 110 110 (10)^(a+2) 11 C> 0^inf in 8a+8b+76 steps, for every a, b and every tape L.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>11</sup> steps
claims.text: Direct C simulation, which also records how far left the head gets in each doubling of the step count.

claims.title: Near misses
claims.text: In the first 3·10<sup>8</sup> steps A reads a 0 followed by 1 1 about 8,500 times (then a 0: no halt), never followed by 1 1 1.

claims.title: A counter that counts down and is reloaded
claims.text: Sampled at the right-end records, the trains sit at fixed places and the head eats the nearest one word per sweep; trips that go further turn the sea they cross into trains, and at step 2,510,806 one trip to the left end reloaded the whole tape (trains of 397, 37, 69, ... words). Read off samples, not proved.

claims.title: No halt in the first 5.03×10<sup>702</sup> steps of an accelerated run
claims.text: Observed, not proved: the accelerated simulator rsim.py ran 5.03×10702 steps from blank tape without reaching a halting transition. Its tape, state and head position were equal to those of a plain C simulator at 6 checkpoints, the last at 1.11×1010 steps. Of these steps, the part after the last checkpoint rests on the simulator alone, including 9,694 trip-level jumps: a jump applies many identical round trips at once after seeing the same tape shape recur with constant count changes, which is validated against direct simulation but not proved.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Open: it halts iff A ever steps onto the front of a train in the wrong phase. An exact macro machine for the trains is the next step.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB---_1LC0LD_1RD0LB_0RF1RE_1RF0RA_0LE0RC up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

check: cd holdouts/1RB0LF_0RC1RD_0LD0RA_1RC0RE_1RF---_1LA0LB && gcc -O2 -o snapR c/snapR.c && ./snapR 1RB0LF_0RC1RD_0LD0RA_1RC0RE_1RF---_1LA0LB 3000000 1 C > s.txt && python3 py/trains.py s.txt

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. Most of this machine's tape is a plain 1010... pattern; the rest is trains of a second pattern, 1110 1110 .... The head eats the nearest train one word per sweep, and now and then a long trip refills every gap with a fresh train: a counter that counts down and is reloaded. Lean proves the machine can only stop if its head steps onto the front of a train in one particular way.

facts.text: A halt needs A stepping onto the front of a train (Lean, kernel).
The sweep that eats one word of a train, for all sizes (Lean, kernel).
No halt in the C simulator.
No halt in the accelerated simulator (observed, not proved; checked against direct simulation up to 1.11×10<sup>10</sup> steps).

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.514).
After 109 steps the tape spans 47,842 cells (14 left of the start, 35,601 right), with a density of 1s of 0.613.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Two seas and the trains
html: Look at the tape late in the run and almost all of it is one of two repeating patterns: the sea 1010..., and stretches of 1110 1110 ..., which we call trains (each 1110 is a word). Short markers separate them. The left end of the tape never moves (cell −14); the right end grows by two cells every sweep.

sections.heading: One sweep eats one word
html: The head sits at the right end and sweeps left, only as far as the nearest train, and back. On the way it flips a single cell: the last word 1110 of the train becomes 1010, so the train is one word shorter and the sea in front of it two words longer. Exactly (Lean, sweep_train, for all a and b):
Each sweep is a little longer than the last (the tape grew), so a train of k words takes about k² steps to eat: the square-root growth of the tape.

sections.heading: A counter that counts down and is reloaded
html: When the nearest train is gone, the head goes on to the next one and eats that, and so on: the trains are like the digits of a counter being counted down. Trips that go further than the nearest train turn the sea they cross into fresh trains. At step 2,510,806 the last train left (5 words, next to the left end) was eaten, and a single trip to the left end refilled every stretch of sea: trains of 397, 37, 69, 9, 13, 12, 15, 13, 7, 2, 2, 2, 2, 3 and 5 words, most a word or two longer than the time before. Such trips are the rare carries of this counter.

sections.heading: Where it could halt
html: The machine stops when E reads a 1. E only follows D reading a 1, D only follows B reading a 1, and B follows either A reading a 0 or F reading a 1 (but F writes a 0 there, which D would then read). So three steps before a halt the head is A on a 0, with 1 1 1 to its right (Lean, halt_needs_A0111): A stepping onto the front of a train, where a word 111 begins.

A reads a 0 followed by 1 1 often (about 8,500 times in the first 3·108 steps), at markers and train edges, but each time a 0 came next. Whether a carry or a reload can ever bring A to the front of a train in the fatal phase is open.

sections.heading: What is proved
html: Lean, kernel: halt_needs_A0111 (lean/Halt.lean); sweep_train (lean/Rules.lean, written by py/gen_rules.py with bbtools.symtm); no halt in 104 steps. native_decide: no halt in 107 steps. C: no halt in 1011 steps; the near-miss count. Heuristic: the counter picture. Open: an exact macro machine and the halting question.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: The tape is a sea of 1010 holding trains of a second sea 1110; the head eats the nearest train one word per sweep and rare trips to the far end reload every stretch of sea as a full train; a halt needs A to step onto the front of a train.
